description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a world-renowned Indian dish featuring succulent chicken pieces in a rich, creamy tomato and butter sauce. This classic recipe delivers an unparalleled depth of flavor, making it a beloved choice for any special meal. Its perfect balance of tanginess, sweetness, and spice will transport your taste buds straight to the heart of India.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, and salt. Mix well to ensure all chicken is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 3-5 minutes per side until lightly browned and cooked through. Remove chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt the remaining 3 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and saute until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Sauce
instructions.text: Add the crushed tomatoes, soaked cashews (drained), 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, and sugar to the pan. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly. Stir occasionally.

instructions.title: Blend and Finish the Sauce
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. You may need to add a splash of water if it's too thick. Pour the smooth sauce back into the pan. Stir in the heavy cream and crushed fenugreek leaves (Kasuri Methi). Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring constantly.

instructions.title: Combine and Serve
instructions.text: Add the cooked chicken pieces to the creamy sauce. Stir gently to coat the chicken evenly. Heat through for 2-3 minutes until the chicken is warmed. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with basmati rice or naan bread.

tips: For an even richer flavor, you can lightly char the marinated chicken pieces in a very hot pan or under a broiler before adding to the sauce.
Do not skip the Kasuri Methi (dried fenugreek leaves); it provides a unique, authentic flavor profile that is essential to classic Butter Chicken.
If you prefer a milder sauce, reduce the amount of Kashmiri red chili powder. For a spicier kick, add a pinch of cayenne pepper.
Ensure the sauce is blended completely smooth for that signature restaurant-style silky texture.
article:
Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a dish that needs no introduction for anyone familiar with Indian cuisine. Its rich, creamy, and subtly spiced tomato gravy, combined with succulent pieces of chicken, has made it a global favorite. This classic Indian chicken recipe is a staple in restaurants worldwide, but its comforting flavors are surprisingly achievable in your home kitchen. Get ready to embark on a culinary journey to recreate the magic of authentic Butter Chicken, a dish that truly embodies warmth and indulgence.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, known traditionally as Murgh Makhani, is an iconic Indian curry that originated in Delhi in the 1950s at the Moti Mahal restaurant. Legend has it that the chefs created this dish to utilize leftover tandoori chicken by simmering it in a rich tomato gravy enriched with butter and cream. The name "Murgh Makhani" literally translates to "chicken with butter," perfectly describing its decadent nature.

At its heart, Butter Chicken is characterized by its velvety smooth, vibrant orange-red gravy. This gravy is typically made from tomatoes, cashews (for richness and thickness), and a delicate balance of aromatic spices like garam masala, ginger, garlic, and fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). The chicken pieces are usually marinated in yogurt and spices before being cooked, contributing to their tender texture and absorbing the flavors beautifully. The dish strikes a perfect balance between tangy tomatoes, a hint of sweetness, and the luxurious creaminess from butter and heavy cream, making it irresistibly delicious and a true comfort food.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken requires a few key components, each playing a vital role in building its signature flavor profile.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch cubes
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt

For the Gravy:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (14.5-ounce) can crushed tomatoes (or 3-4 ripe fresh tomatoes, pureed)
*   1/4 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15 minutes, then drained)
*   1/2 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon sugar (or to taste)
*   1 teaspoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   Salt to taste
*   Water or chicken broth, as needed

For Garnish:
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped
*   A swirl of heavy cream

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to create your own restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for best results.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes, flipping occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through and has a slight char on the outside. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In the same pan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until they turn translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

4.  **Simmer the Gravy:** Stir in the crushed tomatoes, soaked cashews, red chili powder, turmeric powder, and garam masala. Mix well and bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pan and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have softened and the oil begins to separate from the mixture. This indicates the spices are well cooked.

5.  **Blend the Gravy:** Remove the pan from heat and let the mixture cool slightly. Carefully transfer the contents to a blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. For an extra velvety texture, you can pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the clean pan.

6.  **Finish the Gravy:** Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium-low heat. Add the sugar, crushed kasoori methi, and salt to taste. Stir well. Pour in the heavy cream and mix until fully incorporated. Let the gravy simmer gently for 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the gravy to thicken slightly.

7.  **Combine and Serve:** Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering gravy. Stir gently to coat the chicken. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, ensuring the chicken is heated through and has absorbed the delicious flavors of the gravy. If the gravy is too thick, add a splash of water or chicken broth to reach your desired consistency.

8.  **Garnish:** Ladle the hot Butter Chicken into serving bowls. Garnish with a swirl of fresh cream and a sprinkle of chopped cilantro.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-style Butter Chicken at home is all about attention to detail.

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marinating time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight in the refrigerator is ideal.
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Use good quality canned tomatoes or ripe, fresh ones. Kashmiri chili powder offers a beautiful red color without excessive heat. Fresh ginger-garlic paste makes a noticeable difference.
*   **Smooth Gravy:** Blending the gravy until absolutely smooth is crucial. For an ultra-silky texture, strain the gravy through a fine-mesh sieve after blending. This removes any tiny bits of onion or cashews.
*   **Kasoori Methi (Dried Fenugreek Leaves):** This spice is non-negotiable for authentic Butter Chicken flavor. Lightly toast the leaves in a dry pan for a few seconds until fragrant, then crush them between your palms before adding to the gravy.
*   **Balance of Flavors:** Taste and adjust the sugar, salt, and tanginess (from tomatoes) to your preference. A good Butter Chicken has a delicate balance of sweet, tangy, and savory notes.
*   **Don't Overcook Chicken:** Cook the chicken just enough in the initial step, as it will continue to cook in the gravy. This prevents dry, tough chicken.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments, turning a simple meal into a feast.

The classic pairing is with warm, fluffy naan bread or roti, perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich gravy. It also tastes fantastic with steamed basmati rice or a fragrant jeera (cumin) rice. For a complete meal, consider adding a simple side salad or a cooling raita (yogurt dip) to balance the richness of the curry.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect as is, you can easily adapt it to suit different dietary needs or preferences.

*   **Healthier Version:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or substitute some of the heavy cream with milk or coconut milk for a lighter texture. You can also bake or air-fry the marinated chicken instead of pan-frying.
*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** Replace the chicken with paneer (Indian cheese), tofu, or mixed vegetables like cauliflower, potatoes, and peas. For a vegan version, use a plant-based yogurt for marination, coconut oil instead of butter, and full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream instead of dairy cream.
*   **Spiciness:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your liking. For an extra kick, add a finely chopped green chili along with the ginger-garlic paste.
*   **Nut-Free:** If you have a nut allergy, you can omit the cashews. To maintain thickness, you can add a small boiled potato (blended with the gravy) or a teaspoon of cornstarch slurry (cornstarch mixed with a little water) at the end.

Making authentic Butter Chicken at home is a rewarding experience that brings the flavors of India right to your dining table. With this comprehensive guide, you're well on your way to mastering this beloved classic. Enjoy the rich, creamy goodness of your homemade Murgh Makhani!
